examples.solution_text:
The two labelled sides meet at the included angle of $120^{\circ}$.
$\begin{align*} A &= \frac{1}{2}ab\sin C \\ &= \frac{1}{2}(10)(6)\sin120^{\circ} \\ &\approx 26.0\text{ cm}^{2} \end{align*}$

Apply the area rule to each triangle, then add the areas.
$\begin{align*} A_{ABC} &= \frac{1}{2}(10)(6)\sin120^{\circ} \\ A_{ACD} &= \frac{1}{2}(6)(10)\sin120^{\circ} \\ A_{\text{total}} &= \frac{1}{2}(10)(6)\sin120^{\circ}+\frac{1}{2}(6)(10)\sin120^{\circ} \\ &\approx 52.0\text{ m}^{2} \end{align*}$
Keep full calculator precision until the total is rounded.
